source_snapshot.procedure: In BMC WebUI Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs, check DIMM information and detail information.
source_snapshot.criteria: Data should be readable and correct.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES selects only the Processor title, assumes `/redfish/v1/Systems/system/Processors`, disables TLS verification, exposes credentials and returns only member names; it omits the source DIMM Procedure and all detailed identity/topology/status verification.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: FULLY AUTOMATABLE builds a sound complete Processor inventory contract but silently treats the title as authoritative and therefore still drops the explicit DIMM WebUI coverage.

old_problem: Items names Processor while Procedure names DIMM. The prior review treated this read-only target conflict as irreducibly BLOCKED because choosing either target would discard the other. That is unnecessary: both explicit source branches can be retained as separate read-only subtests with independent resources, schemas, topology matrices and acceptance.
disposition_reason: Adopt the conservative union of all explicit source coverage: Subtest A validates Processor inventory from Items; Subtest B validates DIMM information/detail from Procedure. Both must pass independently and retain actual WebUI visual evidence plus protected, service-root-discovered Redfish evidence. This avoids guessing a typo, does not collapse the components, introduces no write, and converts component mappings and expected population into normal Project configuration.
decision_basis: XLSX row 944, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 945 were directly reviewed; the next identity was verified as Functionality row 945 / variant 2b072a9abe8064b1.

Processor and DIMM are both explicit in the protected source. Because both are read-only inventory checks, separate mandatory subtests preserve the union of coverage without the destructive or semantic risk that would make a conservative split invalid.
DMTF Redfish schemas model Processor and Memory as distinct resources. Processor identity/topology/cores/threads/status cannot prove DIMM slot/capacity/type/speed/status, and vice versa.

The generic readable-and-correct Criteria becomes measurable per component by requiring complete member traversal, stable topology identity, schema-valid fields and exact equality to the approved Project hardware/BOM baseline.
ED-02, ED-21, ED-26, ED-33 through ED-38 and the user's no-coverage-reduction rule require separately identifiable coverage rather than choosing or merging one plausible branch.

test_case.test_name: Validate Processor and DIMM inventory as two independent WebUI/Redfish read-only subtests
test_case.purpose: Preserve both conflicting source targets by independently proving that the actual BMC WebUI and authoritative Redfish resources expose complete, readable and correct Processor inventory and complete, readable and correct DIMM inventory against the approved Project topology/BOM, without changing BIOS, power, inventory or logs.
required_package: Target BMC/firmware/WebUI and selected ComputerSystem identity, trusted TLS chain, protected read-only credentials and metadata-redaction rules
Service-root/System-discovered Processor collection and Memory collection links with supported schema versions, pagination rules and member-detail access
Approved Processor baseline: expected socket/population, Id/name, manufacturer/model, architecture/instruction set, core/thread/enabled-core/speed fields, location and Status.State/Health
Approved DIMM baseline: expected socket/controller/channel/slot population, locator, manufacturer/model/part identity, capacity, device/module/memory type, speed/rank/ECC and Status.State/Health
Vendor mapping from both collections and member fields to the actual WebUI Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs tables/detail panels
Raw-response hashing, pagination completeness, absent/disabled/unknown semantics and serial/asset redaction policy
test_case.test_command: READ ONLY. Verify target identity and discover the selected ComputerSystem plus its Processor and Memory links from Redfish rather than assuming `/Systems/system`. Preserve logs. SUBTEST A PROCESSOR: follow the complete Processor collection, every page/nextLink and every member `@odata.id`; retain redacted raw JSON and normalize Id/name, type, architecture/instruction set, manufacturer/model, socket/location, total/enabled cores, threads, speeds and Status.State/Health. Open the actual WebUI Inventory and LEDs Processor table/detail view, capture timestamped visual evidence and compare UI, API and approved socket/BOM baseline field by field. SUBTEST B DIMM: separately traverse the complete Memory collection and every member; normalize Id/name/device locator, location and socket/controller/channel/slot, manufacturer/model/part token, CapacityMiB, memory/device/module type, operating speed, rank/ECC and Status.State/Health. Capture the actual WebUI DIMM table/detail view and compare UI, API and approved slot/BOM baseline. Keep absent, disabled, unknown, unsupported-null, omitted member and request failure distinct. Repeat only read-only fingerprints to prove no change. Do not use `curl -k`, process-visible credentials, names-only output, BIOS/power/inventory writes or log clearing.
test_case.expected_result: Processor subtest enumerates every expected socket/member exactly once with schema-valid complete identity, topology, capacity/performance fields and healthy/expected state matching the Project CPU baseline and WebUI detail. DIMM subtest independently enumerates every expected slot/populated module with schema-valid identity, capacity/type/speed/topology and healthy/expected state matching the Project memory baseline and WebUI detail; expected empty slots follow the approved implementation mapping. Counts, member links, UI rows and normalized matrices reconcile within each subtest, sensitive fields are redacted with traceable tokens, and pre/post fingerprints prove no platform change.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires both subtests independently, complete pagination/member detail, actual WebUI visual correlation, schema-valid normalization and exact comparison to approved component-specific baselines. Processor evidence cannot satisfy DIMM, and DIMM evidence cannot satisfy Processor. Names-only output, assumed URIs, collection count without member details, missing/duplicate sockets or slots, unexplained null/omission, UI/API mismatch or absent authoritative baseline is not PASS. A component documented unsupported may be N/A only with authoritative applicability evidence; otherwise missing mappings/baselines are NOT READY, not Engineering Decision Pending.
safety_gate: Use only protected certificate-verified GET/read operations discovered from the service root; do not use `curl -k`, expose credentials or assume fixed resource IDs.
Do not alter BIOS CPU/memory policy, power state, inventory records, locator LEDs or logs. The broad Inventory and LEDs page does not authorize any control action.
Follow pagination and every member link separately for Processor and Memory; stop on wrong ComputerSystem, schema mismatch, incomplete enumeration or duplicate/missing topology identity.
Keep Processor and DIMM raw data, normalized matrices, WebUI artifacts and verdicts separate. Do not declare the row passed when only one branch is available.
Redact serial/asset identifiers according to Project policy while retaining stable socket/slot tokens and raw-to-normalized hashes needed for audit.
Treat absent, disabled, unknown/null, omitted resource and HTTP/auth/transport failure as distinct states; never populate or change hardware to make inventory appear complete.
expected_evidence: Target BMC/WebUI/ComputerSystem identity, trusted transport, discovered Processor/Memory links, schema versions and approved dual baseline
Complete redacted paginated Processor collection/member responses, normalized socket matrix, exact Project comparison and actual WebUI table/detail visual evidence
Complete redacted paginated Memory collection/member responses, normalized DIMM slot matrix, exact Project comparison and actual WebUI table/detail visual evidence
Per-subtest counts, member/topology reconciliation and distinct absent/disabled/unknown/error interpretation with raw hashes
Read-only audit/no-change fingerprints, explicit two-subtest verdicts and engineer final verdict
test_case.recovery: No mutation is intended. On wrong target, incomplete pagination, schema/topology ambiguity, credential exposure or UI/API mismatch, stop the read-only collection, preserve/redact current evidence and close the session. Do not change BIOS, power, CPU/DIMM configuration, inventory or locator LEDs to repair an observation; obtain the correct schema or Project baseline.

source_conflict.reason: The conflict is resolved without selecting a winner: Items Processor and Procedure DIMM are retained as two separately named, independently accepted read-only subtests. No source statement or component coverage is discarded.

blocked.reason: A safe conservative union is possible because both branches are non-mutating and have authoritative distinct Redfish schemas. Exact resources, UI mappings and expected populations are Project readiness inputs.

external_authorities.title: DMTF Redfish Resource and Schema Guide 2025.3
external_authorities.application: Defines Processor and Memory as separate resources/collections with distinct identity, topology, capacity/performance and status fields.

external_authorities.title: DMTF Redfish Schema Index
external_authorities.application: Describes Processor as a single processor with characteristics/location and Memory as a memory device such as a DIMM, supporting independent schema-driven collection.

project_authority: The Project/vendor package supplies the CPU and DIMM population/BOM baselines, resource/UI mappings, supported-null/absent semantics and redaction policy. It owns each subtest and final DUT verdict; those inputs do not keep the review decision pending.
